question.problem: Find the range of the function $f(x)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{4})-3.$
question.worked_solution:
The range of $\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ is

$$
-1\le \operatorname{cos}⁡x\le 1.
$$

Horizontal shifts and stretches have no effect on the range. Therefore,

$$
-1\le \operatorname{cos}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{4})\le 1.
$$

Multiplying the above inequality by $2$ and then subtracting $3,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & -1\le \operatorname{cos}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{4})\le 1 \\  & -2\le 2\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{4})\le 2 \\  & -5\le 2\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{4})-3\le -1 \\  & -5\le f(x)\le -1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the range is $f(x)\in [-5,-1].$
